# Features

What the port adds or changes compared with the PS3 game (section 1), and how far the port reproduces the game's own features (section 2). Every status rests on a recorded result: a note, a test or a pull request. Anything not listed has not been checked. Options that change gameplay are opt-in. The order of the planned items: [ROADMAP.md](ROADMAP.md).

Port features: 19 available, 17 in progress, 13 planned.

## 1. What the port adds

### Display

| Feature | What it does | State | Default | Setting, notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| <a id="resolution"></a>Higher resolution | Renders at 720p, 1440p, 4K or 5K (5K not tested). Measured in a match on one machine: 1440p about 29.0 and 4K about 28.4 frames per second | available | 720p | RES_SCALE=1..4; [RESOLUTION.md](notes/RESOLUTION.md) |
| <a id="window-fullscreen"></a>Resizable window and borderless fullscreen | The window can be resized; F11 or the launcher's fullscreen option gives borderless fullscreen | available | window | FULLSCREEN |
| <a id="ex-logo"></a>EX in the title logo | The title logo shows EX in place of the +, matching the port's name | in progress | on | JSP_EX_LOGO=0 keeps the +; seen on the title screen in a Windows 11 test, the smaller pre-scaled copy is not yet confirmed |
| <a id="split-screen-layout"></a>Split-screen layout | Larger views and a solo-style HUD in 2-player split screen | planned | - | Parked in the notes |
| <a id="brightness-glare"></a>Brightness and glare | Brightness and glare options | planned | - | Parked in the notes |
| <a id="dlss"></a>DLSS | DLSS upscaling | planned | - | Parked in the notes |
| <a id="wide-screens"></a>Wide and ultrawide screens | 16:10, 21:9 and 32:9 without stretching: a wider view to the sides, the HUD kept at the edges or in a 16:9 box, movies and menus with side bars. Display only | planned | - | A wider view shows more of the arena; ranked may stay 16:9 |
| <a id="vr"></a>VR | A PC VR headset through OpenXR: first the game on a large virtual screen, later the fights in 3D. Research only; needs a steady 60 frames per second first | planned | - |  |
| <a id="fps-counter"></a>FPS counter | The game's own frames per second, bottom left, fading in with the title screen | available | off | FPS_COUNTER=1 or the launcher's “FPS counter (bottom left)” box. US disc only for now: off on the EU disc (it logs “not available on this disc yet”; jsp_region.h). |
| <a id="graphics-options"></a>Graphics options | Edge smoothing (off, FXAA, SMAA), sharpening (off to 100 %), texture filtering (the game's own to 16x), shadow quality (Low to Ultra), shadow distance, model detail and object draw distance, full-size effects. Shadow edges at High and Ultra keep the game's soft-edge width; fights stay at about 29 to 30 frames per second | available | FXAA, Medium, Normal | AA_MODE, SHARPEN, ANISO, SHADOW_SCALE, SHADOW_RANGE, MODEL_DETAIL, OBJECT_DISTANCE, FX_FULL; the settings window's Display and Graphics tabs; compiled and checked on Windows, see [issue #9](https://github.com/Tsamiuy/jsp-vs-ex/issues/9). US disc only for now: off on the EU disc (it logs “not available on this disc yet”; jsp_region.h). That is edge smoothing, sharpening, shadow distance, model detail and object draw distance; texture filtering, shadow quality and full-size effects work on both discs. |
| <a id="two-thread-drawing"></a>Two-thread drawing | The preparing half of drawing runs on its own thread, so busy scenes (3,000 to 4,000 draws a frame) cost less on a slower processor. With the CPU held at its base clock the title demo ran at 28.3 against 26.8 frames per second (about 29.5 with the per-draw cuts of #187); no difference at full speed | available | on | PIPE=0 turns it off; the settings window's “Two-thread drawing” box; on by default since #186; online play with different settings is not tested |
| <a id="present-no-vblank-wait"></a>Frames shown without waiting for the monitor | The port paces itself at 30 frames per second on its own clock and no longer waits for the monitor's vblank as a second clock. On a 60 Hz monitor a frame that took 33 to 50 ms no longer waits for 50 ms, so 30 does not fall to 20 | available | on | D3D12_VSYNC=1 waits for the vblank again, D3D12_VSYNC=0 allows tearing; #185; not tried on a real 60 Hz monitor (a test switch stood in for it) |
| <a id="split-screen-speed"></a>2 Players split screen speed | A 2 Players frame no longer needs two batches with a GPU wait between them, and draws that used few vertices of a big mesh copy only those vertices. A 2 vs 2 on one stage: about 18-24 frames per second before, about 28-30 after, with two-thread drawing on; 1 Player is unchanged | available | on | VPULL_GATHER=0 turns the gathered copies off; measured on one Windows PC only (not a 60 Hz monitor, not online) |
